rationale: Round 5, ADR-conformance lens. I re-read 7404845f from disk, plus internal/panel's Round field and reattest.go; this was read-only. Three of my four round-4 asks are ADDRESSED and one is PARTIAL. On §2(i), the fallback refusals now name an exit that really does change the blocked outcome: the dependent's scoped `--allow-not-ready=MF-3 --evidence` override (R6). The second named exit, the q9ea attested-restore, does not. It restores the bead branch at the candidate's second parent, and R4.2 says the fallback path never identifies a candidate 'whatever ... the surviving tip ... says'. F2 also still refuses on the later unlanded round regardless of the tip. So naming q9ea there points to a step that cannot change the refused fact. There is no deadlock, because the R6 exit remains, but per §2(i) it should not be listed. The audited tuple is correct: the audit must equal the binding pair and the scan-derived candidate, so an audit inherited through MergeMetadata grants nothing. The VALID/MALFORMED shape contract matches R6.3's discipline and is pinned by AC-11 (xiii). Re-running F1–F5 on every read keeps metadata from ever standing in for git facts. The residual is now honestly called a NEW bounded reach rather than 'the same class'. Against the Spec-125 before/after audit rule, the tuple sits beside the existing actor/at/op/corroboration/prior-pair keys in one MergeMetadata call. The forced write when the tuple is absent keeps a record on every acceptance, so the rule is satisfied. The round rule is sound. An anchor is defined by git ancestry to the second parent, so a later unlanded round cannot masquerade as one: if its SHA were an ancestor of the second parent, its work did land. Ties, a missing round (panel.go `Round int`, so 0 for legacy) or no anchor all fail closed, and they have the R6 exit. The only masquerade is a forged `round` value in agent-writable panel.json, and that residual should be stated, as it is for the audit. The staged skill marker now carries a target and a provisional date, and AC-18 pins it. I APPROVE with three narrow text asks.
concrete_changes_required: R4.2 'Exits when a check refuses' and R4.4 arm 1b: remove the ADR-0035 mindspec-q9ea attested-restore from the FALLBACK exits, or state the mechanism by which it changes the outcome. Restoring bead/<id> at the second parent satisfies only F3 (surviving tip). The fallback never auto-identifies on a tip, and F1/F2/F4 refusals are unaffected, so under ADR-0041 §2(i) ('a step that can actually change the fact being refused on') it is not a forward exit here. Keep the R6 scoped-override line as the named exit, and keep q9ea only on the primary-path NoEvidence arm, where it already works. Pin the exit list in AC-11.

R4.2 F2 residual: state that `round` is read from agent-writable panel.json (ADR-0037 §8). A forged high `round` on a stale anchor registration makes a later unlanded round look EARLIER, so F2 passes. Like the audit residual, this is detectable by inspection, not prevented. Add one sentence to the 'Residual, stated honestly' bullets and to the ADR-0041 amendment's F2 text, which AC-18 already pins.

R4.2 audited tuple vs the Spec-125 audit rule ('the corroborating git datum'): specify that on a fallback acceptance the `mindspec_landed_reattest_corroboration` value records the fallback provenance: 'off-first-parent fallback; F1–F5 passed', the scanned panel roots (the F2 visibility line), and the anchor round used. An inspector of the JSONL history can then tell a fallback acceptance from a primary-path one without re-running git.

findings.title: ADR-0041 amendment (audited tuple, round rule) — judged
findings.detail: Touchpoint (i) now enumerates: finder-only; acceptance only by audited reattest after F1–F5 (F2's round ordering, fail-closed cases and visibility limit included); the audited tuple; read-back requiring a VALID audit equal to the binding and the scan-derived candidate plus re-run F1–F5; the bounded-reach residual; withdrawn earlier rules; CLOSE paths first-parent. AC-18's text-pin lists every element. Spec-125 conformance: the existing before/after keys (prior_merge_sha/prior_second_parent) stay, the tuple adds the 'after' identity explicitly, and the no-op write keeps an audit on every acceptance. §2(i): every F refusal has the R6 exit (see ask 1 on q9ea). §2(ii): CLOSE decisions unchanged.

findings.title: q9ea attested-restore named as a fallback exit, but it cannot change a fallback refusal
findings.detail: R4.2: 'lifecycle.FindLandedMergeReachable ... never returns an identified merge for one, whatever the panel set, the surviving tip or the binding says'. The only acceptance is the audited tuple from reattest after F1–F5. q9ea restores bead/<id> at the candidate's second parent, so it changes only F3's input and does not let reattest pass F1 (multiple candidates), F2 (later unlanded round) or F4 (reverted). ADR-0041 §2(i) requires that a named recovery 'can actually change the fact being refused on'.

findings.title: F2 relies on the agent-writable `round` field; this residual is unstated
findings.detail: internal/panel/panel.go: `Round int \`json:"round"\``, read from panel.json. Anchor identity is git-derived, so it cannot masquerade. Round ORDER, though, is metadata: raising a stale anchor registration's round above a later unlanded round flips F2 from refuse to pass. This is the same detectable-by-inspection class as the audit forge, but R4.2's residual bullets cover only the audit and binding.

findings.title: Round-rule attack (can a later unlanded round masquerade as an anchor's ancestor?)
findings.detail: No, by git. An anchor requires reviewed_head_sha to be the second parent or its ancestor, and the second parent is reachable from the tip, so any anchor's work is in the tip's history. A later round whose SHA is outside the tip cannot be an anchor. An in-place round bump (one panel.json reused across rounds) leaves a single registration: if its latest SHA landed it anchors, and if not there is no anchor, which fails closed. Equal-or-ancestor anchoring is required for #233's tree-identical complete commit and is correct. Ties, missing rounds (Round=0 for legacy registrations) and no anchor all fail closed with the R6 exit available, so there is no §2(i) deadlock.
